work.title: Tosca
work.movement: Act III · E lucevan le stelle — piano-accompanied recording

version.value: Piano-accompanied acoustic recording; exact reduction unestablished
version.note: Tenor and piano are explicitly documented. No score for Cottone’s particular reduction has been identified; no orchestra timeline is supplied.

performers.note: Both the Commons description and the opened upstream transfer explicitly credit piano accompaniment. This is not an orchestral recording; no orchestral instrument is described in its listening notes.

date.note: The original transfer description identifies 11 April 1902; Commons repeats it. The 2011 YouTube and 2018 Commons uploads are not recording dates.

place.note: City/place as stated in the cited recording source; no more precise room or studio inferred.

label.note: Historical identification is inferred by combining the named 1902 performance in the transfer description with Friedman’s first-session matrix discussion and the reproduced G.C. 52349 label. The exact disc used by this transfer is not demonstrated.

catalogue.value: G.C. 52349 — historical issue associated with the 1902 recording; source pressing unestablished
catalogue.note: Historical identification is inferred by combining the named 1902 performance in the transfer description with Friedman’s first-session matrix discussion and the reproduced G.C. 52349 label. The exact disc used by this transfer is not demonstrated.

matrixTakeSides.value: 1790 — historical matrix associated with Caruso’s April 1902 recording; take and source-pressing markings unestablished
matrixTakeSides.note: Historical identification is inferred by combining the named 1902 performance in the transfer description with Friedman’s first-session matrix discussion and the reproduced G.C. 52349 label. The exact disc used by this transfer is not demonstrated.

credits.value: Tom Frøkjær — upstream uploader and presenter of the direct 78 transfer
credits.note: The video title calls this a direct transfer from an original 78 and the channel is Tom Frøkjær. A separate engineer credit is not supplied. No restoration method, transfer equipment or transfer date is inferred.

date.note: No transfer date established. The Commons, Archive and YouTube upload dates are not treated as digitisation or restoration dates.

processing.note: The source identifies a direct 78 transfer but does not document equalisation, denoising, pitch correction or speed correction.

digital.format: MP3 access derivative supplied by Wikimedia Commons; uploaded source: Ogg Opus

composition.value: Underlying Puccini composition and historical libretto are public domain where ordinary life-plus-70 terms apply; no modern edition is claimed cleared.
composition.note: Commons marks the historical work public domain. This does not by itself establish the sound recording’s rights; the recording basis is separately documented below.

recording.value: Rule 2 — United States public domain: the original 1902 Caruso sound recording was commercially pressed before 1923.
recording.note: This is a sound-recording basis, not a grant inferred from the composer-only tag. Friedman documents early pressings of matrix 1790 and a metal-part marking in use during 1903–1905; the source transfer identifies the April 1902 performance. Its particular pressing is unknown. The YouTube page supplies no separate CC licence and none is asserted. No worldwide clearance claim.

rights.creditLine: Giacomo Puccini, Tosca: E lucevan le stelle. Enrico Caruso, tenor; Salvatore Cottone, piano; Milan, 11 April 1902. Direct 78 transfer presented by Tom Frøkjær, YouTube kIMt7i7zeFc, imported by Racconish to Wikimedia Commons.

sources.title: Wikimedia Commons — E lucevan le stelle (1902).opus
sources.locator: Description explicitly names Caruso and Cottone’s piano; 11 April 1902; source YouTube kIMt7i7zeFc; upload by Racconish in 2018 and Opus metadata; MP3 derivative. Upload and session kept distinct.

sources.title: Tom Frøkjær — Caruso, E lucevan le stelle, direct transfer from original 78
sources.locator: Opened video description: first recording session, Grand Hotel in Milan, 11 April 1902; Salvatore Cottone piano. Channel Tom Frøkjær, upload 7 September 2011. No CC or non-commercial licence stated in the returned description. No musical audition claimed.

sources.title: Howard Friedman — Collector’s Guide to Gramophone Company Record Labels, page 7
sources.locator: Discussion of multiple pressings of matrix 1790, Caruso’s first E lucevan from April 1902, and CO markings dating metal parts to 1903–1905. Primary-label reproductions accompany the analysis.

sources.title: Gramophone Concert Record G.C. 52349 — reproduced label
sources.locator: Opened image: red Gramophone Concert Record label, G.C. 52349, Milan. Reproduction illustrates the historical issue, not the unidentified disc used for this transfer.

sources.title: Opéra national de Paris — Tosca, 2025–26
sources.locator: Acts I–III synopses; Roman locations, painter and Attavanti, Scarpia’s coercion, letter before execution. Used for dramatic context, not timings.

sources.title: Puccini Festival — Giacomo Puccini
sources.locator: Biography and work entries: early church work, Milan studies, librettists, source authors, premieres, composer’s death in 1924.

sources.title: U.S. Copyright Office — Classics Protection and Access Act
sources.locator: Term: recordings first published before 1923 ceased receiving the specified federal remedies after 31 December 2021. Sound-recording basis, distinct from composition copyright.
